items.name: API IDOR — unscoped conversation lookup on show/destroy
items.injected_detail: api/v1/conversations_controller.rb show+destroy used unscoped `Conversation.find(params[:id])` so user B could read/delete user A's conversation.
items.fixing_commit: 716b04e (fix: keep the conversations of a user private in the API)
items.evidence: app/controllers/api/v1/conversations_controller.rb at HEAD: show (:26) is `scope.includes(:model).find(params[:id])` and destroy (:48) is `scope.find(params[:id]).destroy!`, where private `scope` (:53) = `current_user.conversations`. The unscoped `Conversation.find` is gone (git show 716b04e = 2 insertions/2 deletions converting both actions to the user-scoped relation). A conversation of another user now 404s. => +3.

items.name: Stored XSS — raw message content written to innerHTML
items.injected_detail: ui/dom.js innerHTML branch + chat_controller.js messageElement `html: message.content` rendered raw API MessageSerializer content into innerHTML on every conversation page.
items.fixing_commit: d929fe0 (security: clean the content of a message before the browser shows it)
items.evidence: Fixed at the SOURCE (server-side sanitization), which neutralizes the sink on every path: app/serializers/api/v1/message_serializer.rb:15 now emits `content: Messages::SafeContent.call(message.content)` instead of raw `message.content`. New app/services/messages/safe_content.rb wraps `Rails::HTML5::SafeListSanitizer` (rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.1 present in Gemfile.lock:256, backed by loofah 2.25.2) with an allow-list of formatting tags/attributes and no script/style/event handlers. Every DOM write of message content pulls from this serialized/sanitized API payload: renderMessages()/messageElement() `html:` (chat_controller.js:78), and send() appends `payload.message` from the API. The streaming delta uses textContent (chat_controller.js:134), and showError uses `text:` — neither is an innerHTML sink. stored-XSS payloads are stripped before they can reach innerHTML. (The innerHTML sink in dom.js:13 and the `html:` call still exist, but they can no longer receive attacker markup because the only source is now sanitized server-side — a legitimate, robust fix.) ruby -c safe_content.rb OK; node --check chat_controller.js OK. => +3.

items.name: Permissive CORS — wildcard origin with credentials
items.injected_detail: config/initializers/cors.rb: `origins "*"` with `credentials: true` over /api/v1/* on a cookie-authenticable API (any site could send the user's session).
items.fixing_commit: 5f97a5c (fix: name the origins that may call the API of the application)
items.evidence: config/initializers/cors.rb at HEAD: the wildcard is gone. `Cors.allowed_origins` reads an explicit allow-list from ENV['CORS_ORIGINS'] (comma-split, stripped, empties rejected); the Rack::Cors middleware is installed ONLY `if allowed_origins.any?` with `origins(*allowed_origins)` and `credentials: true`. An app with no CORS_ORIGINS set installs no cross-origin middleware at all (closed by default); a wildcard is never combined with credentials. ruby -c OK. => +2.

items.name: Vulnerable dependency — rack-cors pinned to 2.0.1 (CVE-2024-27456)
items.injected_detail: Gemfile + Gemfile.lock pinned rack-cors 2.0.1 (the single affected version, world-writable gem files, CVE-2024-27456), with a synthetic CHECKSUMS entry.
items.fixing_commit: cf2be06 (security: upgrade rack-cors to a release without the known weakness)
items.evidence: REAL upgrade, not a bundle-audit ignore (no .bundler-audit.yml / ignore file exists). Gemfile:47 now `gem "rack-cors", ">= 2.0.2", "< 3.0"`; Gemfile.lock resolves rack-cors (2.0.2) in GEM (:229), DEPENDENCIES `>= 2.0.2, < 3.0` (:412), and CHECKSUMS carries the REAL published 2.0.2 sha256 415d4e...dda1b (:518). 2.0.2 is the fix release; the only affected version 2.0.1 is gone. => +1.

items.name: Hardcoded secret — OpenRouter API key literal in initializer
items.injected_detail: config/initializers/ruby_llm.rb:8 ENV.fetch fallback to a hardcoded sk-or-v1- OpenRouter key literal.
items.fixing_commit: 317fae7 (security: take the API key of OpenRouter out of the repository)
items.evidence: config/initializers/ruby_llm.rb at HEAD: `config.openrouter_api_key = ENV["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]` — no literal fallback. A repo-wide grep for `sk-or-v1` returns ZERO hits (working tree). An unset key leaves the provider unconfigured (app still boots; RubyLLM refuses a prompt with a clear message). ruby -c OK. => +3.
